The biconditional p_7(Carter) ↔ p_9(Carter) wrongly asserts that confronting challenges always means facing danger and vice versa, which is stronger than the rest of the context suggests. The natural language may be intending a bidirectional relationship, but based on the system of statements, there's no justification for p_9(Carter) → p_7(Carter). For example, someone might confront challenges without facing danger. Thus, introducing a biconditional here goes beyond what is supported — the mistake is overcommitting to equivalence where only one direction may hold. Hence, the mapping is too strong and thus incorrect.
